source.citation: Jin, H., Ghazizadeh, S., Provis, J. L. (2023). Assessment of the thermodynamics of Na,K-shlykovite as potential alkali-silica reaction products in the (Na,K)2O-CaO-SiO2-H2O system. Cement and Concrete Research 172, 107253.

transcription.from: the published article (open-access PDF, CC BY): Table 1 from the text layer, checked against the rendered page; Eqs. (3)-(7) from the text
transcription.note: The PDF ends with the corrigendum of 2024 (Jin2024), which reprints Table 1 with other enthalpies; this file holds the original table, the corrigendum its own file.

entropy_volume_slope.description: S = 1579 Vm + 6, Vm the formula unit volume in nm3, from Eq. (6) of Ghazizadeh et al. (2020) as the paper cites it: the slope.

heat_capacity_volume_slope.description: Cp = 1388.1 Vm + 4.58, from Fig. 2 of Glasser and Jenkins (2011) as the paper cites it: the slope.

log_K_80C_K_shlykovite_cited.description: The solubility product of K-shlykovite at 80 C of Shi and Lothenbach (2019), the paper's reference [22], as the paper quotes it before refining it (Section 3.1, Fig. 1).

log_K_80C_Na_shlykovite_cited.description: The solubility product of Na-shlykovite at 80 C of Shi and Lothenbach (2019), quoted as above.

products.location: Table 1, p. 4: thermodynamic properties of the ASR products at 25 C, estimated by the authors (S and Cp from the formula unit volume, Eqs. (3)-(4); the solubility product refined from the measurements at 80 C of their reference [22] and carried to 25 C, Eqs. (8)-(11)); log_K at 25 C of the dissolution of Eqs. (6)-(7)

dissolution_products.location: Eqs. (6) and (7), p. 2: the dissolution reactions of the solubility products, written with the Cemdata18 symbols of the species (SiO2 = SiO2@, water = H2O@)

notes: The uncertainties of S and Cp are the authors' estimate of 10 %, propagated by them to the enthalpy and the Gibbs energy (footnote a of Table 1).

The entropies and heat capacities follow from Eqs. (3)-(4) with Vm = V/N_A: 0.3039 and 0.2723 nm3 give 485.8 and 436.0 J/(mol K) for S, 426.4 and 382.6 for Cp, the tabulated values to 0.1; the printed Vm (0.3, 0.27) are those rounded.

The Gibbs energies reproduce the solubility products through the aqueous species of Cemdata18 (the database of the paper, Section 2.1): log K at 25 C recomputed -31.19 and -34.82 against the printed -31.2 and -34.8.

With the element entropies of the Cemdata18 ThermoFun file, dfG + T (S - sum of the element entropies) at 298.15 K gives -5736.3 and -5839.3 kJ/mol: the enthalpies of this table agree with the Gibbs energies and entropies to 0.1 and 0.5 kJ/mol. The corrigendum (Jin2024) replaces them by -5163.6 and -5267.5 kJ/mol, which differ from that relation by +572.7 and +571.8 kJ/mol, the Gibbs energies and entropies being unchanged; recorded as found.
